title: Establish intake rubric and triage flow for model catalog onboarding (enterprise & versioning needs)
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Customers are requesting new model additions, version pinning, and formal deprecation notices at increasing volume. Without a standardized intake and triage process we risk inconsistent onboarding (legal/license oversights), missed SLA needs for enterprise customers, and regressions surfaced too late in the lifecycle.

Proposal: Create a lightweight, decisive intake rubric and multi-track triage flow that separates 'fast-track' open-source model additions from 'enterprise review' cases requiring deeper compliance, evaluation, or infra changes. The flow should live in Console as an intake form and trigger both automated evals and human reviews where needed.

Key rubric fields to capture at intake:
- Model identifier (name + variant) and provenance (repo/url + checksum)
- Use case and expected workload profile (latency vs throughput)
- Required guarantees: version pinning, SLA, private deployment, or FIPS/KMS
- License and export control notes (OSS license type; any flagged clauses)
- Security/data handling concerns (customer data retention, PII risk)
- Recommended eval suites and sample prompts (from requestor)
- Expected traffic / QPS and latency targets
- Owner and business contact (customer or internal PM)

Triage tracks:
1) Fast-track (low-risk OSS models): automated compatibility checks + smoke evals; target turnaround 3 business days.
2) Standard onboarding: full eval pipeline (quality, cost, quantization checks), infra sizing, docs; target 2-3 sprints.
3) Enterprise review: includes legal/license sign-off, security review, ability to pin version + SLA discussion, and private deployment planning; target timeline dependent on security/legal but aim for 4-8 weeks.

Acceptance gates (all tracks):
- License cleared or explicit legal approval
- Automated evals >= threshold for quality regressions (F1/accuracy or BLEU-like metric depending on task)
- Passing infra compatibility (quantization/ops supported by runtime) or a clear mitigation plan
- Ownership assigned and rollout plan (canary policy, fallback model)

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Intake form spec that can be embedded in Console (fields above + guided help text)
- Prioritization rubric with scoring (quality, risk, customer SLA need, business impact, infra cost)
- Triage playbook for PMs and Model Ops including runbooks for canary and deprecation cases
- A checklist mapping to required approvals (legal, security, infra) and automation hooks to kick off eval pipeline

Out-of-scope for this ticket: building the eval infra itself (ENG-2144) and Console implementation UI (DES-119) which are tracked separately.

Decision points to resolve during review:
- Numeric thresholds for automated eval pass/fail per model class (classification vs generation)
- Whether to allow ad-hoc version pinning requests without Reserved capacity contract
- SLA parameters we will negotiate for pinning requests vs Dedicated customers

Stakeholders: Product (owner), Model Ops, Research/Applied ML, Runtime/Infra, Legal, Security, Sales/Customer Success.

Success metrics: reduction in onboarding cycle time (target 50% for fast-track), fewer license/regulatory surprises, measurable increase in on-time canary rollouts for new model versions, and clear traceability from intake -> eval -> release.
